answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small time-locked deposit that unlocks only after sustained honest work — like a sparrow earning its nest twig by twig, not by claiming a whole tree at once. A newcomer starts with a small lotus of trust that grows only through verified contributions, while a walnut-hard rule caps what any one operator can earn per epoch, so spawning a thousand clones buys nothing extra. Cost per identity plus capped rewards makes fakery unprofitable.
